newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: NWE oil products gain, fuel oil may have bottomed.
newsitem.headline: NWE oil products gain, fuel oil may have bottomed.

text.p: NWE oil products all firmed on Thursday, with fuel oil rising on a growing sentiment that the market may have bottomed out, dealers said.
Gasoline was up by around $1 a tonne to a range of $219/$221 fob AR. One deal was rumoured done at $218 fob AR, a level which traders said was surprisingly low.

Heating oil gained $3 a tonne, principally on IPE gas oil futures strength. Offered premiums for prompt loadings rose 50 cents to Feb IPE +$3.50 fob ARA, but traders said it was hardly justified as buying showed no sign of improvement and ice continued to lock up canals in Germany.

High sulphur fuel oil barges added about $3 a tonne with a deal at $98 fob ARA and later offers at $99, although bids were more plentiful than offers. Traders said bunker demand was noticeably improved as shipowners increasingly suspected the market may have bottomed out.
"All those who were bearish are bullish now," one trader said.
However, fuel oil stocks in the ARA area remained high.
